method: Visual inspection of the four fixed original grayscale CT sections with earlier model maps hidden. Dark and bright bands are described by appearance without assigning sheet identity.
control: PHerc0139 w035 stored native CT, row 32. A bright band can be followed from left to right near the origin, with modest depth variation.

sections.finding: On the right, several dark bands bend below the negative depth boundary toward the centre. The distinct band around d=-9 to -15 at local x=160,192,224 does not establish a connected central sheet across the left and right halves.

A strong dark band lies near d=0 to +1 around local x=96 and 128, and around d=+4 at x=160. It coexists with another dark band on the negative side around d=-16 to -23. The central band cannot be assigned to sheet, gap, or boundary from this section.

A short dark band around d=+3 to +7 at local y=64,96,128 changes strength and fades or splits. Several contrast bands remain in other depth ranges. A sheet through the centre cannot be linked across both ends.
Several adjacent wavy bands are visible at negative and positive depth and bend or fade at different places. The centre does not supply a continuous uniquely identifiable band.

conclusion: Current geometry adoption threshold not met. Physical sheet correspondence and a constant offset are indeterminate. Multiple contrast bands are visible, and no sheet switch or multiple physical sheets has been established.
independent_review: Lead independently reviewed sections.png without prior model images. Lead could trace the bright w035 band and could not uniquely trace the same PHerc1218 sheet near d=0 in three or more sections. The central Y2204 dark band remained unclassified.
next_discriminator: A physical trace through the orthogonal original CT that links both sides of the same papyrus lamina across the fixed crop, independently identifies gap and sheet, and can be intersected with P+dN. A fixed offset test needs consistent signed depths along that trace.
